add-056.title: Harissa Chili Paste
add-056.culturalNotes: Harissa is a hot chilli paste from Tunisia and the Maghreb, used with grills, soups and couscous. The layer of oil on top protects it from air so it keeps longer.

instructions.1: Wash and dry the chillies, cut into small pieces, and remove the seeds to reduce the heat if you like.
instructions.2: Blend the chillies, garlic and spices until fine.
instructions.3: Add the salt and lemon, then the olive oil gradually with the blender running until creamy and smooth.
instructions.4: Pack into a sterilised glass jar, cover the top with a layer of olive oil and keep refrigerated for up to a month.

add-057.title: Sautéed Chicken Livers with Onion and Pepper
add-057.culturalNotes: Chicken livers cook quickly and overcooking makes them dry and rubbery. If the centre is light pink they are done.

instructions.1: Wash the livers with water, salt and lemon, trim the membranes and veins, and drain well.
instructions.2: Heat the oil and brown the onion until golden, then add the garlic and pepper for a minute.
instructions.3: Add the livers on high heat and turn until coloured on all sides.
instructions.4: Add the spices, salt, pepper and pomegranate molasses and cook on low heat just 5 minutes until done but not dry.
instructions.5: Squeeze over the lemon and serve with Arabic bread or rice.

add-058.title: Quick Homemade Roumi-Style Cheese
add-058.culturalNotes: This is a quick home version that resembles roumi cheese in taste and look, but it is not an aged cheese. Keeps wrapped in the fridge for a week.

instructions.1: Blend the oil, egg yolks, vinegar, water, milk powder, cornflour and salt until smooth with no lumps.
instructions.2: Add the cheese triangles and keep blending until they melt completely.
instructions.3: Grease a heatproof metal or glass container with oil and dust with starch; pour in half the mixture, scatter the peppercorns, then add the rest.
instructions.4: Cover with its lid and foil and cook in a water bath (a pot of boiling water halfway up the container) for an hour, topping up the water as it reduces.
instructions.5: Let cool, then chill overnight before unmoulding and slicing.

add-059.title: Syrian Shakriyeh (Lamb in Yogurt Sauce)
add-059.culturalNotes: Shakriyeh is a Damascene dish for special occasions. The secret to yogurt that doesn't split: cornflour and egg, stirring constantly in one direction until it boils, and salting at the end.

add-059-i1.name: Lamb (shanks or pieces on the bone)

add-059-i6.name: For boiling: bay leaves, cinnamon stick, cardamom, whole onion

add-059-i8.name: Ghee and toasted pine nuts or almonds to garnish

instructions.1: Simmer the meat in water with the aromatics, skimming the foam, for 1-1½ hours until tender; drain and keep a cup of the broth.
instructions.2: Sauté the sliced onion in a spoon of ghee until soft and translucent.
instructions.3: Whisk the yogurt with the cornflour and egg until completely smooth, in the cooking pot itself.
instructions.4: Put the yogurt over medium heat and stir constantly in one direction, without stopping, until it boils, so it doesn't split.
instructions.5: Add the onion, meat, cup of broth and salt and simmer 10 minutes, stirring.
instructions.6: Serve in a deep dish topped with pine nuts toasted in ghee, with vermicelli rice.

add-060.title: Aden-Style Lamb Zurbian
add-060.culturalNotes: Zurbian is one of the best-known dishes of Aden in Yemen. It resembles biryani but relies on plenty of dark fried onion and a long yogurt marinade.

add-060-i1.name: Lamb or beef on the bone

add-060-i8.name: Ground cardamom, black pepper and cinnamon

add-060-i11.name: Whole spices for the rice (cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, bay leaf)

instructions.1: Marinate the meat with the yogurt, garlic, ginger, ground spices, salt and half the fried onion for at least 2 hours.
instructions.2: Cook the meat with its marinade in a covered heavy pot on low heat with a little water for 45-60 minutes until nearly tender.
instructions.3: Lightly fry the potatoes and add them to the meat for the last 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Boil the rice in salted water with the whole spices until 70% cooked, then drain.
instructions.5: Spread the rice over the meat in the pot and sprinkle with the saffron, ghee and remaining fried onion.
instructions.6: Cover tightly on very low heat for 25 minutes, then smoke with an ember on a piece of foil with ghee inside the pot for 10 minutes.
instructions.7: Turn the zurbian out onto a large platter to show the meat and potatoes and serve with spicy bisbas salsa.

add-061.title: Fig and Strawberry Tart
add-061.culturalNotes: Very cold butter and not kneading are the secret to a crisp shell. The shell is blind-baked first so the cream doesn't make it soggy.

add-061-i9.name: For the cream: cornflour and sugar

instructions.1: Rub the flour, icing sugar and salt with the cold butter until sandy, add the yolk, vanilla and iced water and bring together without kneading; chill 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Roll out and line the tart tin, prick with a fork and chill 15 minutes, then bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes with weights (rice or beans on baking paper) for the first 15 minutes, until golden.
instructions.3: For the cream: heat the milk, whisk the yolks with the sugar and cornflour, add the hot milk gradually, return to the heat stirring until thick, add the vanilla and cover with cling film until cool.
instructions.4: Whip the cold cream, then fold the cold custard into it gently.
instructions.5: Spread the cream into the cooled tart shell and arrange the sliced figs and strawberries on top.
instructions.6: Brush the fruit with the melted apricot jam to glaze and chill the tart an hour before serving.

add-062.title: Bahraini Shrimp Biryani
add-062.culturalNotes: Removing the seeds of the dried lime prevents bitterness. The shrimp are seared quickly at first and finish in the steam with the rice so they stay tender.

add-062-i3.name: Turmeric and biryani or fish spice

add-062-i4.name: Lemon juice and salt for marinating

instructions.1: Marinate the shrimp with the garlic, ginger, turmeric, spice, lemon and salt for 15 minutes.
instructions.2: Sear the shrimp in a spoon of oil on high heat for just 2 minutes until they colour, then remove.
instructions.3: Fry the onion in the remaining oil until golden, add the tomatoes, paste, dried lime and chilli and cook until the sauce thickens, then return the shrimp with the coriander.
instructions.4: Boil the rice in salted water until 70% cooked and drain.
instructions.5: Spread the rice over the sauce, sprinkle with saffron and a little ghee, and cover the pot tightly on very low heat for 20 minutes.
instructions.6: Fluff the biryani gently and serve with green salad and lemon.

add-063.title: Homemade Coconut Chocolate Bars
add-063.culturalNotes: Chilling the coconut slab before cutting gives clean edges and easy coating. You can press an almond onto each bar before coating.

add-063-i3.name: Melted white chocolate for the filling

instructions.1: Mix the coconut with the condensed milk by hand until absorbed, then add the 2 tbsp white chocolate to bind.
instructions.2: Spread the mixture between two plastic sheets on a tray into an even rectangle (about 1.5 cm thick) and chill 15-20 minutes.
instructions.3: Cut into even bars, or roll into small balls if you prefer.
instructions.4: Dip the pieces with a fork into the dark or white chocolate, let the excess drip, and place on baking paper.
instructions.5: Drizzle with lines of the contrasting chocolate, chill until set and keep refrigerated.

add-064.title: Kunafa Cups with Strawberries and Cream
add-064.culturalNotes: Toasting the kunafa with icing sugar gives it a golden colour and a crunch that lasts longer under the cream. Mango or berries can replace the strawberries.

instructions.1: Crumble the frozen kunafa finely by hand and mix with the ghee and icing sugar.
instructions.2: Toast in a wide pan on low heat, stirring constantly, until golden and crisp, then spread out to cool completely.
instructions.3: Whip the Chantilly powder with the cold milk, sugar and cream cheese until thick.
instructions.4: Build the cups: a layer of kunafa drizzled with a little syrup, then cream, then strawberries, and repeat.
instructions.5: Top with strawberry slices and a sprinkle of kunafa, and serve within a few hours so it stays crisp.

add-065.title: Pink Pickled Turnips
add-065.culturalNotes: Beetroot gives the natural pink colour of Levantine pickled turnips. Coarse salt and a little sugar keep them crunchy.

instructions.1: Wash, peel and cut the turnips into fingers or half-moons, and slice the beetroot.
instructions.2: Pack the turnips into a sterilised jar with beetroot and garlic slices between the layers to spread the colour.
instructions.3: Dissolve the salt and sugar in the cooled water and add the vinegar.
instructions.4: Pour the brine to cover the turnips completely and weigh them down with a beetroot slice or small weight so they don't float.
instructions.5: Close the jar and leave in a cool place 3-5 days until pink and tangy, then refrigerate.

add-066.title: Levantine Makdous (Oil-Cured Stuffed Eggplant)
add-066.culturalNotes: Makdous is one of the most important preserves in Syria and Lebanon. Success depends on removing all the water from the eggplant and peppers, as any left will cause mould.

add-066-i3.name: Sweet red peppers, minced and drained

instructions.1: Remove the eggplant stems, leaving the small green cap, and wash.
instructions.2: Boil the eggplants in salted water for 8-10 minutes until tender but not mushy, then drain.
instructions.3: Slit each eggplant lengthwise, put a little coarse salt inside, and lay them slit-side down in a colander under a weight for 24-48 hours until all the water is out.
instructions.4: Squeeze the minced red pepper very well and mix with the walnuts, garlic, hot pepper and salt.
instructions.5: Stuff each eggplant with the mixture and press to close.
instructions.6: Pack tightly into sterilised jars, lay the jars on their side for a day to drain any remaining water, then cover completely with olive oil, seal and leave two weeks before eating.

add-067.title: Egyptian Mfatteka (Molasses & Sesame Sweet)
add-067.culturalNotes: Mfatteka is a traditional Egyptian sweet given to nursing mothers in winter because it is full of energy. It keeps in sealed jars outside the fridge for weeks.

instructions.1: Toast the sesame, peanuts and nigella seeds in a cup of the oil over low heat, stirring, until fragrant.
instructions.2: Add the ground fenugreek and stir 2 minutes without burning.
instructions.3: Add the molasses and stir constantly over low heat for 15-20 minutes until it thickens and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
instructions.4: Add the remaining oil and stir, then pour into dishes, garnish with crushed peanuts and leave to cool.

add-068.title: Chicken Drumsticks in Yogurt-Ketchup Marinade
add-068.culturalNotes: Covering the tray at first keeps the chicken juicy, and uncovering at the end gives the skin its glossy red colour.

add-068-i8.name: White or black pepper and paprika

instructions.1: Clean the drumsticks, soak 15 minutes in salted water, rinse and dry, and score deeply so the marinade penetrates.
instructions.2: Mix the remaining ingredients, toss the drumsticks in it and chill 2-4 hours.
instructions.3: Arrange in a tray, cover with foil and bake at 200°C for 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Remove the foil, brush with the remaining marinade and bake another 15 minutes until browned, turning once.
instructions.5: Serve with rice or roast potatoes and salad.

add-069.title: Yemeni Saltah (Sanaa Style)
add-069.culturalNotes: Saltah is the favourite everyday dish of Sanaa, served still boiling in a stone pot called a 'madra'. The whipped fenugreek is its soul.

add-069-i1.name: Hot rich meat or chicken broth

add-069-i8.name: For sahawiq: fresh coriander, garlic, chilli and salt
add-069-i8.standardAmount: a bunch + 2 cloves + 2 chillies + a pinch

instructions.1: Soak the fenugreek in water for at least an hour, pour off the water and whip with a blender or whisk, a little cold water and the sahawiq until it becomes a light white foam.
instructions.2: For the sahawiq: grind the coriander with the garlic, chilli and salt.
instructions.3: Sauté the onion in the oil, then add the tomatoes, paste and chilli and cook down (the kishna), adding the minced meat or egg if using.
instructions.4: Heat a stone pot (madra) or heavy pot until very hot and pour in the broth with the kishna and vegetables until it boils hard.
instructions.5: Spoon the fenugreek foam over the top while it bubbles and serve at once in the pot with malawah or lahoh bread.

add-070.title: Pickled Eggplant with Garlic and Pepper
add-070.culturalNotes: Garlic-pickled eggplant is a popular Egyptian side for ful and taameya. Squeezing out the water after boiling keeps them firm in the brine.

instructions.1: Boil the eggplants whole with their caps in salted water for 8-10 minutes until slightly soft, then drain and cool.
instructions.2: Slit each eggplant lengthwise without separating, press gently to release the water, and leave in a colander for an hour.
instructions.3: Mix the garlic, chillies, coriander, cumin, a little salt and the olive oil and stuff the slits.
instructions.4: Pack the eggplants in a sterilised jar, mix the vinegar, water and salt and pour over to cover.
instructions.5: Close the jar and leave in a cool place 5 days before eating, then refrigerate.

add-071.title: Spicy Gulf Dakkous Salsa
add-071.culturalNotes: Dakkous is the constant companion of Gulf rice dishes because its sharpness cuts the richness of the meat. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

instructions.1: Cut the tomatoes into large pieces and put in the blender with the garlic, chilli and coriander.
instructions.2: Add the lemon, vinegar, tomato paste and salt.
instructions.3: Pulse in short bursts until smooth but still with small pieces, not a juice.
instructions.4: Chill 10 minutes and serve with kabsa, mandi and grills.

add-072.title: Cherry Jam
add-072.culturalNotes: Citric acid adds tartness and helps the jam set and keep. Dark cherries give the most beautiful colour.

instructions.1: Wash the cherries, remove the stems and pit them with a cherry pitter or the end of a straw.
instructions.2: Dissolve the sugar in the water over medium heat, then add the cherries.
instructions.3: Boil over medium heat, skimming and stirring now and then, for 30-40 minutes until thick.
instructions.4: Add the citric acid five minutes before removing from the heat, and test by dropping a little on a cold plate — it should not run.
instructions.5: Pour the hot jam into sterilised jars and seal at once.

add-073.title: Homemade Fresh White Cheese
add-073.culturalNotes: This fresh cheese is close to Egyptian areesh and Indian paneer and needs no rennet. Use the leftover whey in dough or soup.

instructions.1: Heat the milk, stirring, until it starts to boil.
instructions.2: Turn off the heat and add the lemon juice gradually, stirring gently, until the milk separates into white curds and yellow-green whey; leave 5 minutes.
instructions.3: Pour into a sieve lined with cheesecloth and rinse with cold water to remove the lemon taste.
instructions.4: Add the salt and nigella seeds and mix, then gather the cloth and squeeze gently.
instructions.5: Put a weight on the cloth for 2 hours in the fridge until set into a block, then slice; keeps 4 days refrigerated.

add-074.title: Indian Chicken Masala
add-074.culturalNotes: Garam masala is made from spices that are toasted and then ground; the toasting gives its deep aroma. Increase the chilli to taste.

add-074-i12.name: Garam masala (toasted, ground coriander, pepper, cumin, cardamom, cloves)

instructions.1: Marinate the chicken with the yogurt, half the ginger, half the garlic, 1 tsp chilli and half the salt for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Sauté the onion in the ghee until golden, then add the remaining garlic and the hot chillies.
instructions.3: Add the tomatoes, sugar, masala, remaining chilli and salt, and the vinegar, and simmer until the tomatoes break down into a thick sauce.
instructions.4: Add the chicken with its marinade, stir, cover and cook 10-12 minutes until done.
instructions.5: Stir in the cream for a minute and serve with basmati rice or naan.

add-075.title: Chunky Strawberry Jam
add-075.culturalNotes: Cooking uncovered lets the strawberry juice evaporate and concentrates the flavour. The jam thickens more as it cools, so don't cook it until very stiff.

instructions.1: Hull, wash and drain the strawberries and cut into small or medium cubes.
instructions.2: Put the strawberries and sugar in an uncovered pot over medium heat until plenty of juice comes out, then lower the heat.
instructions.3: Add the cinnamon stick and stir now and then until the liquid reduces and the colour turns deep red.
instructions.4: Add the lemon and raise the heat slightly, stirring constantly so it doesn't catch, and test on a cold plate — it should hold its shape.
instructions.5: Remove the cinnamon and pour the hot jam into sterilised jars and seal.

add-076.title: Karnıyarık (Turkish Stuffed Eggplant)
add-076.culturalNotes: Karnıyarık means 'split belly' in Turkish. This version roasts the eggplant in the oven instead of frying, so it is lighter.

add-076-i8.name: Black pepper, paprika and ground coriander

instructions.1: Soak the halved eggplants in salted water for 15 minutes, dry them and score the white flesh in a crisscross.
instructions.2: Place white side up in a tray, brush with oil, sprinkle with salt and roast at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until soft and coloured.
instructions.3: Sauté the onion, then the garlic and peppers, then add the meat until it breaks up and cooks, then half the tomatoes, the spices and salt until the juices dry.
instructions.4: Press the centre of each eggplant half with the back of a spoon to make a hollow, fill it and top with the remaining tomatoes.
instructions.5: Pour the tomato juice thinned with a little water around the eggplants and return to the oven for 20 minutes.
instructions.6: Garnish with coriander and serve with rice or yogurt.

add-077.title: Homemade Tomato Ketchup
add-077.culturalNotes: Ketchup thickens more as it cools, so take it off the heat when a spoon leaves a clear line on the bottom of the pot. The vinegar and sugar are what preserve it.

instructions.1: Cook the tomatoes and peppers with the water in a covered pot for 15 minutes until completely soft.
instructions.2: Blend until smooth, then pass through a fine sieve to remove the skins and seeds.
instructions.3: Return the juice to the pot with the vinegar, sugar, spices and salt.
instructions.4: Simmer uncovered on low heat for 40-45 minutes, stirring often, until thick like ketchup.
instructions.5: Let cool, then bottle in a sterilised bottle and refrigerate for up to 3 weeks.

add-078.title: Levantine Hummus Fatteh
add-078.culturalNotes: The secret of hummus fatteh is the contrast between hot chickpeas, cold yogurt and crisp bread, so assemble it just before serving.

add-078-i9.name: To garnish: parsley, pomegranate, toasted nuts (pine nuts or almonds) and paprika

add-078-i10.name: Ghee or butter for toasting the nuts

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas overnight in plenty of water, then rinse.
instructions.2: Simmer in fresh water until very tender (60-90 minutes, or 25 minutes in a pressure cooker), keeping a little of the cooking water.
instructions.3: Fry the bread cubes in oil until golden and drain, or brush with oil and toast in the oven.
instructions.4: Whisk the yogurt with the tahini, lemon, garlic, cumin and salt until smooth.
instructions.5: Spread the bread in a deep dish, moisten with a little hot chickpea water, then add the hot chickpeas, then the yogurt sauce.
instructions.6: Toast the nuts in the ghee and pour sizzling over the fatteh; garnish with parsley, pomegranate and a pinch of cumin or paprika and serve at once.

add-079.title: Chocolate Bird's Nest Kunafa
add-079.culturalNotes: Bird's nest is a Levantine kunafa sweet traditionally filled with pistachios. Chocolate is sweet on its own, so a light drizzle of syrup or none at all is enough.

add-079-i6.name: Ground pistachios or icing sugar to garnish

instructions.1: Separate the kunafa strands and brush with ghee, then wrap each thin strand two or three times round your finger into a small nest and tuck the end underneath.
instructions.2: Pack the nests close together in a greased tray and press each centre slightly to make a hollow.
instructions.3: Brush with the remaining ghee and bake at 180°C for 15-20 minutes until golden and crisp.
instructions.4: Drizzle with a little syrup if you like and let cool slightly.
instructions.5: Fill each nest with a spoon of chocolate spread, top with hazelnuts and sprinkle with pistachios or icing sugar.

add-080.title: Swiss Roll with Jam and Cream
add-080.culturalNotes: Rolling the cake while hot gives it a 'memory' of the rolled shape, so it doesn't crack when filled once cool.

instructions.1: Whisk the eggs with the sugar, vanilla and vinegar for 8-10 minutes until doubled, pale and thick.
instructions.2: Sift the flour with the baking powder and fold in gently with a spatula in batches so it doesn't deflate.
instructions.3: Spread in a rectangular tray lined with greased baking paper and bake at 180°C for 10-12 minutes until springy.
instructions.4: Turn the cake straight onto a clean towel dusted with icing sugar, peel off the paper and roll up with the towel while hot; leave to cool rolled.
instructions.5: Unroll gently, spread with jam then cream, roll again and chill 30 minutes.
instructions.6: Dust with icing sugar and cut into slanted slices.

add-081.title: Homemade Spreadable Cream Cheese
add-081.culturalNotes: The longer you process it, the smoother it gets. Add dried herbs, garlic or chopped olives for different flavours.

instructions.1: Heat the milk over medium heat until almost boiling.
instructions.2: Turn off the heat, add the lemon juice and stir gently for a short while until the milk separates into white curds and liquid.
instructions.3: Pour into cheesecloth set over a bowl and let the whey drain 1-2 hours until the curds are a little dry.
instructions.4: Process the curds in a food processor with the butter, salt and 2 tbsp of whey until completely smooth and creamy.
instructions.5: Pack into an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 5 days.

add-082.title: Easy Budget Vanilla Cupcakes
add-082.culturalNotes: Vinegar with baking powder gives these cupcakes a good rise with just one egg, and the cornflour makes them softer.

add-082-i6.name: Milk with a spoon of yogurt

instructions.1: Whisk the egg with the vinegar and vanilla until frothy, add the sugar and whisk until dissolved.
instructions.2: Add the oil, then the milk with yogurt, and mix.
instructions.3: Sift the flour, baking powder, cornflour and salt and add gradually, mixing until smooth.
instructions.4: Fill lined cupcake cases two-thirds full and bake at 180°C for 18-20 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
instructions.5: Let cool and decorate with cream or chocolate sauce as you like.

add-083.title: Two-Layer Milk and Orange Mahalabia
add-083.culturalNotes: Waiting for the first layer to set before pouring the second is the secret of clean, separate layers.

instructions.1: Dissolve the starch and sugar in the cold milk, then stir over medium heat until thick and boiling for a minute; add the orange-blossom water.
instructions.2: Divide among cups or a serving dish and leave until cool and the surface sets.
instructions.3: Dissolve the starch and sugar in the cold orange juice with the zest and stir over heat until thick, glossy and clear.
instructions.4: Let it cool a little, then pour gently over the milk layer using the back of a spoon so the layers don't mix.
instructions.5: Chill 3-4 hours and garnish with orange slices or pistachios.

add-084.title: Lentil Soup Fatteh
add-084.culturalNotes: Lentil fatteh is an Egyptian way to turn lentil soup into a full meal; the garlic-vinegar topping gives it the familiar fatta flavour.

add-084-i11.name: Butter, chopped garlic and vinegar for the topping

instructions.1: Put the lentils, vegetables, garlic, stock cubes, spices and water in a pot, bring to the boil and simmer 30 minutes until everything is cooked.
instructions.2: Blend the soup until smooth and adjust the thickness and salt.
instructions.3: Fry the chopped garlic in the butter until golden, then carefully add the vinegar and let it bubble a minute.
instructions.4: Put the toasted bread in deep bowls, pour the hot soup over, then the garlic-vinegar topping, and serve with lemon and spring onion.

add-085.title: Turkish-Style Basbousa (No Eggs, No Butter)
add-085.culturalNotes: Resting the semolina with the milk for an hour gives this basbousa its sandy texture even without butter or eggs, making it much lighter than regular basbousa.

add-085-i6.name: Syrup: sugar, water and lemon
add-085-i6.standardAmount: 1½ cups sugar + 1¼ cups water + a squeeze of lemon

instructions.1: Boil the sugar, water and lemon for 10 minutes and leave the syrup to cool.
instructions.2: Mix the semolina, sugar and baking powder, add the milk and fold gently without kneading until combined.
instructions.3: Spread in a greased 25 cm tin, level and leave 1-1½ hours for the semolina to absorb the milk.
instructions.4: Cut into squares and place a peanut on each piece.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C with bottom heat until the edges brown, then top heat until the surface colours.
instructions.6: Pour the cold syrup over as soon as it leaves the oven and let it soak.

add-086.title: Mixed Fruit Jam
add-086.culturalNotes: Apples are rich in natural pectin, helping the jam set without additives, and the mandarin gives it a fresh aroma.

instructions.1: Wash, peel and cut the fruit, removing the mandarin seeds.
instructions.2: Blend the fruit with the cup of water into a purée (or leave some pieces if you like).
instructions.3: Cook the purée with the sugar in a pot over medium heat, stirring, until boiling, then lower the heat.
instructions.4: Cook 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick, adding the lemon before removing from the heat.
instructions.5: Pour hot into sterilised jars and seal.

add-087.title: Egyptian Cooked Hot Chili Sauce
add-087.culturalNotes: This is the chilli sauce served with koshari and ful in Egyptian restaurants. Cooking it with vinegar and oil makes it keep a long time, and the heat depends on how many hot chillies you use.

instructions.1: Cut both kinds of pepper, remove the seeds and mince in a processor with the garlic into a paste.
instructions.2: Heat the oil in a pot, add the minced peppers and stir over medium heat until the water evaporates.
instructions.3: Add the vinegar, salt and sugar and simmer 20-25 minutes, stirring, until thick and the oil rises to the top.
instructions.4: Let cool, pack into clean jars with a layer of oil on top and refrigerate for months.

add-088.title: Levantine Fried Kibbeh
add-088.culturalNotes: Iced water on your hands stops the dough sticking and keeps the wall thin without cracking. Kibbeh can be frozen raw and fried straight from frozen.

add-088-i4.name: Salt, black pepper, cumin and a pinch of cinnamon for the dough

add-088-i5.name: Coarse minced meat for the filling

add-088-i6.name: Onions, finely chopped, for the filling

add-088-i8.name: Allspice, salt and pepper for the filling

instructions.1: For the filling: soften the onion, add the coarse meat and stir until it breaks up and cooks, then add the spices and pine nuts and let cool.
instructions.2: For the dough: process the lean meat with the onion and spices into a paste, then add the bulgur in batches and process or knead with hands dipped in iced water until the dough is smooth and holds together.
instructions.3: Take a ball the size of a small egg and hollow it with your index finger, turning it on your palm until the wall is thin and even.
instructions.4: Fill with the stuffing, close and shape into an oval with pointed ends, wetting your hands with iced water.
instructions.5: Deep-fry in hot oil in batches for 4-5 minutes until dark golden and crisp, then drain.
instructions.6: Serve with cucumber yogurt or lemon.

add-089.title: Syrian Maarouk (Sweet Ramadan Bread)
add-089.culturalNotes: Maarouk is a sweet bread tied to Ramadan in Syria and Lebanon, and mahlab is the soul of its flavour. It can be filled with coconut or chocolate or left plain.

add-089-i10.name: Filling: date paste with cinnamon and butter

add-089-i11.name: For the top: egg yolk, milk, sesame and nigella seeds

instructions.1: Mix the dry ingredients with the mahlab and anise, add the milk, yogurt and butter and knead 10 minutes into a soft, fluffy dough.
instructions.2: Cover and leave an hour or more until doubled.
instructions.3: Knead the date paste with the butter and cinnamon and roll thin between two sheets.
instructions.4: Divide the dough, roll each piece into a rectangle, lay the date paste on it and roll up, then shape into a braid, ring or round as you like.
instructions.5: Leave 30 minutes to rise again, brush with the egg yolk and milk, sprinkle with sesame and nigella and bake at 180°C for 15-20 minutes.
instructions.6: Cover with a cloth as soon as they come out so they stay soft.

add-090.title: Cheese-Stuffed Luqmat al-Qadi
add-090.culturalNotes: Freezing the cheese cubes for 15 minutes before filling stops them melting too fast and leaking into the oil. The salty cheese with sweet syrup is what makes this version special.

instructions.1: Mix the dry ingredients, add the oil and warm water gradually and beat by hand into a smooth, sticky batter; cover an hour until doubled.
instructions.2: Heat the oil over medium heat.
instructions.3: Take a little batter in your palm, push a cheese cube into the middle, squeeze a ball out between thumb and index finger so the batter wraps the cheese, and drop it into the oil with a wet spoon.
instructions.4: Turn the balls constantly until golden and crisp all over.
instructions.5: Drain and dip at once in the cold syrup or drizzle with honey, and serve hot with the cheese melted.

add-091.title: Indian Potato Samosa
add-091.culturalNotes: Frying on medium-low heat is the secret to the crisp, blistered crust of authentic Indian samosa.

add-091-i11.name: Turmeric, curry, paprika, ground coriander and cumin

add-091-i14.name: Chutney sauce (mint, coriander, chilli and lemon)

instructions.1: Mix the flour, cumin seeds and salt, rub in the oil until sandy, add the water and knead into a smooth, slightly firm dough; cover 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Sauté the onion, then the garlic, ginger and chilli, add the spices for a minute, then the potatoes, peas and salt, mashing lightly; add the coriander and lemon and let cool.
instructions.3: Divide the dough into 8 balls, roll each into an oval and cut in half, shape each half into a cone, fill and seal the edge with water.
instructions.4: Fry slowly in medium oil for 8-10 minutes until golden and crisp with small bubbles on the crust.
instructions.5: Serve hot with green chutney or tamarind sauce.

add-092.title: Egyptian Sakhina (Bread in Molasses and Ghee)
add-092.culturalNotes: Sakhina is a winter breakfast in rural Egypt that gives warmth and energy. Stale, dry bread works best as it soaks up the molasses without turning mushy.

instructions.1: Mix the molasses with the water and half the ghee in a pot over medium heat until boiling.
instructions.2: Spread the bread pieces in an oven tray or clay dish.
instructions.3: Pour the hot molasses over the bread until absorbed, then dot the rest of the ghee on top.
instructions.4: Bake at 200°C for 10-15 minutes until the bread absorbs all the liquid and the top browns slightly.
instructions.5: Sprinkle with sesame and serve hot.

add-093.title: Cheese Stuffed-Crust Pizza
add-093.culturalNotes: Sealing the edge well around the cheese stops it leaking during baking. Cheddar or cheese triangles can replace the mozzarella in the crust.

add-093-i3.name: Warm water to activate the yeast

add-093-i12.name: Green pepper, tomato and olives for the top

instructions.1: Activate the yeast in the warm water with the sugar for 5 minutes, add to the flour, salt, garlic powder, oil and remaining water, knead 10 minutes until smooth and let rise an hour until doubled.
instructions.2: Divide the dough in two and roll each into a circle 3 cm larger than the tray on every side.
instructions.3: Lay the cheese sticks around the edge and fold the dough edge over them inwards, pressing firmly to seal.
instructions.4: Prick the base with a fork, spread with sauce and top with grated cheese and vegetables.
instructions.5: Bake in a very hot oven (240°C) for 15-20 minutes until the crust browns and the cheese melts.
instructions.6: Brush the crust with a little garlic-parsley butter and serve hot.

add-094.title: Chicken Ranch Pizza
add-094.culturalNotes: Ranch is a creamy American herb dressing, and dill gives it its signature flavour. It keeps a week in the fridge and is great with salads and potatoes.

add-094-i3.name: For the ranch: garlic powder, onion powder, dried dill and dried parsley

add-094-i4.name: For the ranch: salt and black pepper

add-094-i10.name: Chicken breast cubes, seasoned and sautéed

instructions.1: Mix the ranch ingredients well and chill 30 minutes so the flavours blend.
instructions.2: Knead the dough ingredients with the warm milk until smooth and let rise an hour until doubled.
instructions.3: Sauté the chicken seasoned with salt, paprika and garlic until cooked.
instructions.4: Spread the dough in two greased trays and spread with a layer of ranch instead of tomato sauce.
instructions.5: Scatter the cheese, chicken and vegetables, then a final sprinkle of cheese.
instructions.6: Bake at 230°C for 15-20 minutes and drizzle with lines of ranch after baking.

add-095.title: Frothy Lemon Mint Lemonade
add-095.culturalNotes: Blending peeled lemons briefly prevents bitterness, and the two spoons of milk give the pale colour and thick froth known from juice shops.

add-095-i4.name: Very cold water or sparkling water

instructions.1: Peel the lemons and remove all the seeds and as much of the thick white pith as possible so the juice isn't bitter.
instructions.2: Blend the lemons, mint, sugar, half the water and the ice for only 30 seconds.
instructions.3: Strain through a fine sieve, return to the blender with the remaining water and the milk and blend a few seconds until frothy.
instructions.4: Pour at once over ice and garnish with mint leaves and a lemon slice.
